newsitem.title: UK: NatWest's Wanless said Owen departure mutual.
newsitem.headline: NatWest's Wanless said Owen departure mutual.

text.p: National Westminster Bank Plc's chief executive Derek Wanless said he had not fallen out with Martin Owen, the NatWest Markets investment banking head who resigned on Monday.

"Martin and I had been talking for some time and it had become pretty clear that we should part company. When we looked at what NatWest Markets needed going forward, we felt the need to change the leadership of the business," Wanless told Reuters.
"It was obvious to me and to Martin that something needed to be said because clearly there seemed to be rumours around which certainly weren't factually correct."

"As often happens with these things it was something that we both agreed on," Wanless said, adding the decision about Owen's departure after five years at the helm of NatWest Markets had been made relatively recently.
Wanless said Owen was on a 12-month rolling contract and details of what sort of package he would get had not yet been finalised.
NatWest Market's overall performance, the various issues it has faced and the need to bring together the various businesses it had acquired had prompted the change in management.
"It seemed important we strengthened the management at NatWest Markets to make sure that we capitalised on the excellent businesses we have put together over the last couple of years," he said.

Asked why this had not happened so far, Wanless would not lay the blame on Owen. But he said getting to grips with the 77 million stg losses on interest rate options, which surfaced in February, had been a considerable distraction.

"When we look at what's being done...a lot of the things which are possible going forward relate to the acquisitions we made only last year. So its obviously fairly early days to develop the business overall," Wanless said.
"What we see the need for is getting the integration working between the businesses and making sure that we think through very carefully the efficiency of capital deployment of the business."
While this was something that was a continual part of running the business, NatWest Markets now had "a number of excellent businesses that we can start to run together", Wanless said.
